notes: §1985:VII.4.7.4 GR16: "If the ADVANCING phrase is not used, automatic advancing will be provided by the implementor to act as if the user had specified AFTER ADVANCING 1 LINE", then items a-h for the phrase. WriteRecord reroutes a WRITE without the phrase to WriteAdvancingRecord (1 line, AFTER) whenever SupportsVerticalPositioning holds, which is now a LINAGE clause or AdvancingDeclared, set from the OPEN for a file whose program writes any ADVANCING phrase (PB5201), closing this row's old gap for a plain WRITE before the first ADVANCING write; BindAdvancing/ScreenAdvancingCount bind and screen the operand, FeatureAdvancing gives a mnemonic-name its feature's rule, and Position, PositionOnLogicalPage, BeginNextLogicalPage, Advance, WriteTravel and Present carry items a, c, d, e, f, g and h. Probes at 85 (work-rs-04/c9, bytes read back): plain, plain, AFTER 1, plain gives a line feed before every record; BEFORE 2, BEFORE 1, AFTER 1, AFTER 3, plain place each record as a-f require; 0 / ZERO / identifier 0 overprint (c); AFTER/BEFORE PAGE without LINAGE write a form feed (h); C01 mnemonic acts as PAGE (d); a negative identifier takes the PAGE arm (b, undefined); on LINAGE 4 TOP 1 BOTTOM 1 AFTER PAGE and BEFORE PAGE reach line 1 of the next logical page, LINAGE-COUNTER 2, 4, 1, 1, 1, 2 (g); an 18-digit identifier is clamped at 2147483647 lines (an implementation limit, f); -1, 1.5, PIC 9V9 COBOL2365 and BEFORE AFTER refused (b, c, rows c3). The witness runs LINAGE-COUNTER through a, c, g and the omitted phrase and reads back a mixed print file. || kb/Work PB5570 (landed): an EXTERNAL file's print-file fact is the connector's, so the binder shares it across every describing unit of the compilation group (ExternalFileConnectorRules.ShareAdvancing) and a plain WRITE before the unit that names ADVANCING is first activated is AFTER ADVANCING 1 LINE (witness 1985-GR-VII_4_7_4-16-external). Remaining PARTIAL: an EXTERNAL describer compiled APART from the group is reached only by the run time's merge at its registration (FileRegistry.Register), so plain WRITEs made before that separately compiled program is activated are still bare records.
